records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:23 — P2, confidence 100: `var self = this, offset = Math.min(this.get("user_count"), Math.max(this.get("offset"), 0));` clamps against the stale pre-request count, so removing the sole member from the last page reloads that now-out-of-range offset and leaves the administrator on an empty page despite members remaining on earlier pages.
records.rationale: The finding describes a real bug in the pagination logic. Looking at the diff in group.js lines 21-23: `var self = this, offset = Math.min(this.get("user_count"), Math.max(this.get("offset"), 0));` - this clamps the offset against the current `user_count` BEFORE making the request. When a member is removed from the last page, `removeMember` calls `findMembers()` which uses the stale `user_count` to clamp the offset. If you're on page 2 (offset=50) with 51 users and remove the last one, the server returns the new count (50), but the request was made with offset=50 (clamped against old count 51)
